purpose: Backend registry of reusable blueprints and major data-layer entry points. A blueprint defines fields, sources, normalization rules, temporal models, relationships, integrity constraints and refresh logic inherited by concrete records.
inheritance_rule: Concrete records store observations and relationships; instructions belong to the parent blueprint.

coverage_model.rule: Every major recurring entity family should inherit a dedicated blueprint or an explicit named section of a structural blueprint. New domain-specific blueprints are preferred when the field model becomes deep enough to warrant independent acquisition, validation and relationship logic.

automation_rule: Blueprints are executable specifications. Acquisition jobs read them to discover fields, sources, refresh intervals, validators, derived measures and relationship templates. Missing data is recorded as missing, never silently fabricated.
frontend_rule: Backend depth must be reachable through a small set of human-readable hubs. Raw registries are not themselves the primary navigation experience.
expansion_rule: Blueprints are additive ontology infrastructure. They may be extended when a domain has distinct entities, temporal logic, evidence requirements, relationship types or derived measures that cannot be cleanly represented by a generic structural pattern.
